Under continuous and bounded probability distributions, the optimal trimming set geometry in trimmed K-means transitions from a union of equal-radius spherical balls to anisotropic ellipsoidal boundaries if and only if the objective function incorporates a Mahalanobis dispersion penalty matrix $\Sigma_j^{-1}$ per cluster $j$.

The universal finite-sample breakdown point of robust K-means algorithms utilizing proximal alternating minimization is bounded by $O(1/n)$ under arbitrary contamination, but can be elevated to a constant fraction $\Omega(1)$ if the underlying data distribution satisfies a robust geometric separation condition ((ρ1, ρ2)-balance).

A parametric extension of pseudo-isolation score distributions using extreme value theory yields closed-form tail bounds that asymptotically dominate Cantelli-based nonparametric thresholds in multi-dimensional contaminated spaces.

Deterministic multi-scale geometric trimming via convex relaxations of anisotropic dispersion tensors can achieve bounded approximation ratios for non-spherical trimmed k-means without requiring exhaustive stochastic search heuristics.

Replacing running-sample empirical nonparametric estimates with closed-form parametric asymptotic distributions for multi-dimensional pseudo-isolation scores will tighten tail probability bounds and reduce false-alarm rate calibration error under skewed data distributions.

Integrating minimum-covariance-determinant (MCD) estimators into pseudo-isolation score and dispersion calculations preserves outlier detection precision better than Median Absolute Deviation (MAD) rules when feature spaces experience severe multi-directional contamination.

Deploying non-spherical trimmed K-means frameworks across high-dimensional domain benchmarks without dimensionality reduction yields higher cluster purity and classification accuracy compared to standard spherical trimmed formulations.

Integrating non-parametric false-alarm rate calibration and automated pseudo-isolation score thresholds into applied clustering loops eliminates the need for manual trimming proportion specification while maintaining robust outlier detection across heterogeneous contamination rates.

Replacing simple scale estimators (such as MAD) with robust minimum-covariance-determinant (MCD) estimators in outlier-trimmed K-means pipelines significantly reduces false-alarm rate inflation and preserves precision in contaminated high-dimensional IoT intrusion detection settings.
